brief.purpose: A family garden with somewhere to eat outside and space for the kids.

concepts.name: Somewhere to walk to
concepts.summary: A smaller terrace at the doors and a second place at the far end worth the walk, with the route to it slightly indirect and the planting deepening as you go.

issues.message: Front path ends at nothing in particular.
10% of the garden is open grass, where a concept of this kind wants at least 20%.
the garden store is 12.9 m from the side gate, past the 8 m it wants. The bins and the mower come in from the street, so the store belongs by the side gate.
8 different materials, where a modern plan wants at most 3.
Only 13% of the garden is under canopy, against about a third in a designed plan.

explanation.rationale: A garden built round one generous open lawn, organised around the terrace area. The terrace and play areas are what this concept is not worth offering without.

decisions.text: Somewhere to walk to. 16 m is far enough for the far end to be its own place rather than the back of the lawn.
Chosen from 13 arrangements of this garden, on circulation, grouping and how the space is proportioned.
Laid 3 paths beside the lawn and a walk down the view rather than a path across the grass to each room.
Put the fire pit at the end of the view from the doors, so the eye has somewhere to land.
Made the fire pit the reason to go out, at the far end past the lawn and reached down its side.
Kept the garden store in a far corner, on the gate side, out of the view from the doors.
There was no bay for a second seating area that did not mean standing it on the lawn.
Put the seating patio directly outside the garden doors, 9.0 × 3.6 m.
Play area at the far end of the lawn, where it can be seen from the house.
Dining pergola in the dining area, at the end of the terrace, so each room has its own floor.
Garden store in the utility corner, on the gate's side, where the bins and the mower can reach it without crossing the lawn.
Fire pit in the far corner of the garden, at the far end, on the diagonal from the doors.
Kept the lawn as one continuous panel rather than cutting it into pieces.

concepts.name: Terrace and lawn
concepts.summary: A terrace across the doors, one clean lawn set off-centre so the planting runs deeper down one side, and the gathering places in the far corner.

issues.message: Front path ends at nothing in particular.
The lawn has 3 inside corners and 1.7× the outline a compact shape of its area would have: it is the ground left over rather than a shape.
the garden store is 12.9 m from the side gate, past the 8 m it wants. The bins and the mower come in from the street, so the store belongs by the side gate.
The dining area is what this concept is organised around, and Seating patio is larger.
Nothing terminates the view down the garden from the doors.
8 different materials, where a modern plan wants at most 3.
Dining pergola sits under 0.3 m from the boundary, too tight to build against or maintain.
Only 10% of the garden is under canopy, against about a third in a designed plan.

explanation.rationale: A garden built round eating and entertaining outside, organised around the dining area. The terrace and play areas are what this concept is not worth offering without.

decisions.text: Terrace and lawn. A terrace, a gap and a rear border leave 4.6 m of lawn, which reads as a strip.
Chosen from 13 arrangements of this garden, on circulation, grouping and how the space is proportioned.
Notched the lawn round one room rather than standing it on the grass.
Laid 3 paths beside the lawn and a walk down the view rather than a path across the grass to each room.
Put the play area at the end of the view from the doors, so the eye has somewhere to land.
Kept the garden store in a far corner, on the gate side, out of the view from the doors.
There was no bay for a second seating area that did not mean standing it on the lawn.
Put the seating patio directly outside the garden doors, 9.0 × 4.3 m.
Play area at the far end of the lawn, where it can be seen from the house.
Dining pergola in the dining area, at the end of the terrace, so each room has its own floor.
Garden store in the utility corner, on the gate's side, where the bins and the mower can reach it without crossing the lawn.
Fire pit in the far corner of the garden, at the far end, on the diagonal from the doors.
Kept the lawn as one continuous panel rather than cutting it into pieces.

concepts.name: Sweeping lawn
concepts.summary: A flowing lawn that bulges and narrows between deep planted bays, with a path that curves out of sight to a seat at the far end.

issues.message: Path to the shed cuts through a planting bed.
Front path ends at nothing in particular.
23% of the designed ground is curved or angled in a plan that is otherwise straight: open gravel, a planting bed, a planting bed.
the garden store is 12.9 m from the side gate, past the 8 m it wants. The bins and the mower come in from the street, so the store belongs by the side gate.
6 different materials, where a modern plan wants at most 3.
This garden asks for more looking after than a low-upkeep brief allows: 40% of what a garden can demand, against 35%.
Only 10% of the garden is under canopy, against about a third in a designed plan.

explanation.rationale: A garden built round deep planting and somewhere quiet to sit in it, organised around the terrace area. The terrace and play areas are what this concept is not worth offering without.

decisions.text: Sweeping lawn. Deep planted bays either side of a lawn that opens out towards the far end.
Chosen from 13 arrangements of this garden, on circulation, grouping and how the space is proportioned.
Laid 2 paths beside the lawn and a walk down the view rather than a path across the grass to each room.
Put the fire pit at the end of the view from the doors, so the eye has somewhere to land.
Kept the garden store in a far corner, on the gate side, out of the view from the doors.
Put the seating patio directly outside the garden doors, 9.0 × 3.6 m.
Play area at the far end of the lawn, where it can be seen from the house.
Dining pergola in the dining area, at the end of the terrace, so each room has its own floor.
Garden store in the utility corner, on the gate's side, where the bins and the mower can reach it without crossing the lawn.
Fire pit in the far corner of the garden, at the far end, on the diagonal from the doors.
Laid one open panel of gravel where a lawn would have been, since none was wanted.
